Only ITGB2 was sequenced (Sanger); no other genes or exclusion of other causes reported. Cohort-level: the authors say the LAD1+ patients with this variant presented later in life with pyoderma gangrenosum-like skin lesions, and CD11a was reduced in 8 of 10 LAD1+ cases.

Based on the CD18 expression on neutrophils, LAD1 was sub-classified into three phenotypes viz. severe (LAD1°) with CD18 expression <2% moderate (LAD1^-) phenotype with CD18 expression 2%–30%, and mild (LAD1^+) phenotype with CD18 expression ≥30%.
Molecular confirmation was performed was done using Sanger sequencing for LAD1 and next-generation sequencing (NGS) for LAD3.
50% of LAD1^+ had a splice site mutation.
These patients presented later in life with recurrent skin lesions like pyoderma gangrenosum.
All of them had the same c.1224+4A>G mutation and 4 of these patients have been reported by us earlier (39).
Although the expression of CD18 was >30% in LAD1^+ cases, the CD11a was significantly reduced in 80% (8/10) of the cases.
On the other hand, splice site mutations affected almost 60% of LAD1^+ patients.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: From the batch HGVS: intronic variant at a splice region (canonical or near-canonical position); protein effect not predicted (p.?). Table S2 gives type 'Splice site', Intron 10, domain '-'. Mechanism in the paper is general: the LFA-1 alpha subunit is not expressed without the beta subunit. For LAD1+ patients (all with this variant) the authors suggest partial CD18 expression may underlie the skin lesions.

quotes.quote: It is known that α- subunit of LFA-1 cannot be efficiently expressed unless it first associates with the β subunit.

Though the pathogenesis of these inflammatory lesions is not clear, partial expression of CD18 resulting in an aberrant oscillation of integrins on the neutrophil surface and Th17 mediated aberrant inflammatory response may be responsible for these inflammatory skin lesions (40, 41).

authors_classification.statement: Cohort-level only: the authors call the 57 ITGB2 variants of Table S2 'disease-causing' and say 35 were novel. No per-variant classification or ACMG criteria. Table S2's references column for this variant reads 'CS151559'.

quotes.quote: Direct Sanger sequencing of the ITGβ2 gene revealed 57 disease-causing variants in 105 patients (Table S2), including 30 patients we have previously reported (18).
We identified 57 mutations in 105 patients of which 35 were novel suggesting heterogeneity in the mutation spectrum for LAD1.

concerns: Single source: a multicentre retrospective cohort (Kambli 2020, PMID 33391282); per-person genotypes come only from Supplementary Table S2, which gives no transcript and no genomic coordinates.
The paper says 30 of its patients were reported before in its ref 18 (Madkaikar 2015, PMID 25703682) without naming them, so carriers here may be the same people as in that paper.

Table S2's '#' marks are inconsistent: P23, P63 and P76 carry one '#'-marked and one unmarked variant, 12 patients are '#'-marked in all, while the text says compound heterozygous variants were found in only 10 patients.
No parental or family testing is described for LAD1 (the family-testing sentence in the methods refers to NGS for LAD3); Table S1 has a Family History column but no genotyped relatives.

All five carriers are LAD1+ (CD18 >=30%); the paper says 4 of them were reported earlier in its ref 39 (Madkaikar 2015, PMID 25876705) without naming which, so same-person duplicates with that paper are likely.
P20, P28 and P29 have family history 'Yes'; relatedness among the five is not stated (127 cases came from 125 families).

The text says '50% of LAD1^+ had a splice site mutation. ... All of them had the same c.1224+4A>G mutation', but elsewhere 'splice site mutations affected almost 60% of LAD1^+ patients', and P63 (LAD1+) carries a different splice-site variant (c.1658-2A>G).
Not a canonical splice-site position (+4); no RNA or splicing study is reported.
Table S2's references column reads 'CS151559' rather than 'Novel' or a GenBank number, which may point to an earlier report not identified in this paper's text.
notes_for_panel: All evidence comes from one multicentre Indian cohort (PMID 33391282): genotypes from Supplementary Table S2, clinical rows from Supplementary Table S1. No segregation, de novo, phase or variant-level functional data are reported; the CD18 flow-cytometry subtype is the only per-person laboratory finding. Zygosity is per-person only through Table S2's '#' marks, which are inconsistent.
